subject: Throughput relief & trial extension proposal — Orexis Retail
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@orexis.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Orexis Retail Billing <billing@orexis.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: High latency during checkout simulation — urgent

Hi Alex,

We ran a scaled checkout simulation this morning (saw it peak around 3,000 concurrent requests) and observed repeated tail latency spikes from the Redwood API. Several requests to the /generate endpoint were returning in 8–12s instead of the usual ~200–400ms which caused a queue pile-up on our side. This is blocking our Black Friday readiness testing.

Can you share whether there was any degraded capacity or a known regression on your side between 08:30–09:10 PST? We need an ETA for mitigation and also to understand what sort of service remedy you can provide — our operations and procurement teams will want to know next steps and any credits or trial extension you can apply while we finish testing.

Appreciate a prompt reply.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Reliability
Orexis Retail

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@orexis.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:29:47 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency during checkout simulation — urgent

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I'm opening an incident now and looping in our on-call infra lead (Marissa) to investigate the 08:30–09:10 window.

Prelim steps:
- We'll pull request traces + server-side latency histograms and share an initial incident summary within 2 hours.
- As an immediate remediation gesture while we investigate, we're prepared to provision a token top-up and a 30-day trial extension to give your test team headroom.
- If a sustained regression is confirmed on our side we will follow our SLA remediation playbook (billing credit + token compensation).

Can you confirm the account org id we should use for the token grant (or confirm we can top up to the API key used by ops@orexis)? Also, are there any billing contacts we should CC on the formal credit note?

I'll be back with an initial post-mortem summary shortly.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 10:38:10 -0800
Subject: RE: High latency during checkout simulation — urgent

Alex / Aditya — I pulled the node-level telemetry and request traces. Summary (high level):
- Between 08:32–08:58 PST we observed an anomalous scheduling delay on a subset of instances serving the gpt-4x-realtime model family. The scheduler's batching window increased due to an unfortunate interaction with a new kernel selection heuristic we rolled out last week.
- Impact: ~12% of requests during the window saw tail latency in the 6–12s range, overall p95 moved from 410ms to ~1.1s for the period. No data exposure — purely latency.

Recommended customer remediation package:
1) Immediate: grant 150k tokens to the Orexis org (to their existing API key) to allow uninterrupted testing today.
2) Credit: apply a one-time billing credit equal to 25% of November usage for the affected service (capped at $12,000).
3) Trial extension: 30-day extension on their trial/PO window so they can finish Black Friday testing without pressure.
4) RCA: attach a short incident report and commit to a permanent kernel-heuristic rollback + canary for next release.

I've prepared a short incident report (attached) and a draft credit terms PDF that legal/finance can sign off on. I think the package above is reasonable given the impact and our internal SLOs; it aligns with similar gestures we've made for comparable outages.

Attachments: incident_report_20251105.pdf (application/pdf)

If you want to be more generous (exec ask), we can increase token grant to 250k tokens or raise the credit cap to $18k, but I'd prefer to start with the proposal above and escalate if Orexis pushes back.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Incident Response Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@orexis.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Orexis Retail Billing <billing@orexis.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 11:05:22 -0800
Subject: Proposal: token grant + billing credit + trial extension

Hi Elena — thanks again for flagging this and for your patience while we investigated.

Summary of what we can offer immediately to support your Black Friday readiness testing:
- Token grant: 150,000 tokens applied to the API key that your ops team used today (please confirm the key or org id).
- Billing credit: one-time credit equal to 25% of November usage tied to the affected service, capped at $12,000.
- Trial extension: 30-day extension on your evaluation/PO term.
- RCA & fix: attached is our incident report; we'll roll back the kernel heuristic and add a targeted canary in the next 48 hours.

If that package is acceptable, I'll start the internal approval and route the credit terms for signature (DocuSign link below). Once signed we can apply the credit and token grant the same day.

DocuSign (credit terms): https://docusign.example.com/link/ORX-CR-2025
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ORX-2025-1472

Please reply here with the API key/org id to top up and confirm billing contact for the credit memo.

Best,
Alex

From: Elena Torres <elena@orexis.com>

Cc: Orexis Retail Billing <billing@orexis.com>

Alex — the proposal looks fair, thank you. Please:
1) Apply the 150k tokens to API key: ops-blackfriday-03 (org id ORX-99823).
2) Route the credit terms to billing@orexis.com and cc me.
3) Send an incident RCA once available — our platform team wants a short summary they can attach to their runbooks.

We accept the package as outlined. If you can expedite the token grant today that would be ideal — we'll resume testing after that.

Regards,
Elena
